known_defects: The diffs follow the diff settings of the person's git (corrected in 0.2.3).
Untracked links are read through, and the executable bit of an untracked file is not covered (corrected in 0.2.4).
`--report-only` still writes a rejected finding to `docs/reviews/decisions.md`, and a review without a task file updates and archives `task.md` (corrected in 0.1.4).
An untracked file is hashed the way git would store it: with `core.autocrlf=true`, a change from LF to CRLF leaves the fingerprint the same (corrected in 0.6.1).
The commit is not part of the fingerprint: a clean tree at another commit gives the same four hashes (corrected in 0.6.1).
A submodule is not looked into: what changes in one that is dirty already is not seen, and on Windows neither is a junction in its place that is pointed elsewhere (corrected in 0.6.1).
Nothing in an untracked folder that is a git repository of its own is covered: a change there leaves the four hashes the same (corrected in 0.6.1).

A tracked file reaches the fingerprint only through git's status and diffs, so a change that git does not report leaves the four hashes the same: other line endings in a file that is modified already, with `core.autocrlf=true`; a change of the same size in text that a clean filter drops; or an edit to a file marked with `git update-index --assume-unchanged` (corrected in 0.6.2).

mechanisms.mechanism: The check that the reviewer changed nothing is four commands in the skill's text, run in the folder the session was started in. The fourth lists untracked files with `git ls-files --others`, which lists only the files below the current folder. Started in a subfolder, the check does not see an edit to an untracked file anywhere else in the repository: new code under review can be changed unnoticed.
mechanisms.trigger: Claude Code started in a subfolder of the repository; an untracked file outside that subfolder is edited between the two checks.
mechanisms.why_severity: A definite gap in the check, met whenever a session starts below the root.
